indian_entity: The Ayurvedic canon in Arabic (Caraka, Susruta, Madhavanidana, Astangahrdaya)
chinese_source: EXTERNAL Arabic anchor: Ali ibn Rabban al-Tabari, Firdaws al-Hikma (Paradise of Wisdom), completed c. 850, part VII
event: Al-Tabari closes his medical encyclopedia with a 36-chapter summary of Indian medicine drawn from four named books: Charaka (Jarak), Susruta (Susrud), the Nidana (Niddin = Madhavakara's Rugviniscaya) and the Astangahrdaya (Ashtanqahrada)
date_raw: Composed at the court of al-Mutawakil, c. 849-850
firmness_reason: A dated, extant work; Meyerhof's identification of the four Arabic titles with the four Sanskrit works is the standard reading (Isis 16, 1931; Siggel's 1951 edition of the Indian chapters)
notes: One dated page brackets four canon texts at once: Caraka, Susruta, Madhava (c. 700) and Vagbhata's Hrdaya all existed in Arabic-accessible form by 850. The earliest datable Arabic attestation of Caraka's content.
references: Siggel, Die indischen Bucher aus dem Paradies der Weisheit (1951)
